segments.text: Why do people travel to Kashi, also called Varanasi, to be freed of their sins? The answer begins with Brahma, the creator, who once had five heads. Shiva cut one off in rage. Then it would not let go of him. It began with a curse. The sage Narada had said Brahma would desire what must not be desired. When Brahma created his daughter Brahmi, the curse took hold. She saw his gaze and moved away. Each time she moved, a new head grew so he could keep looking at her. His sons Marichi and Atri warned him. Brahmi became a cow, a mare, a duck, a doe, a hundred forms in all. She was named Shatarupa. Shiva appeared in fury. Brahma came to his senses and begged forgiveness. Shiva cut off the fifth head. Brahma's four mouths would recite the Vedas forever to repent. Then Shiva stopped. The severed head was stuck to his left hand. Killing a Brahmin was a sin. Atri said every action brings its result, whatever the reason. Brahma had paid, though a curse drove him. So must Shiva. Shiva wandered the universe, but nothing freed him. The flesh rotted away until only a skull remained. He was called Kapali. Then he reached a place on Earth, and the skull fell from his hand. Anyone who came there would be freed of every sin. That place became Kashi, also called Varanasi, and that is why people still go there.
